clue.text: Tinkers seizing buses in riotous mischief-making

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it, as a hand seizing something grips it

parts.note: to monkey with something is to tinker with it, so tinkers gives monkeys

indicators.note: a riotous crowd is disordered, so the letters of buses in are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Travelling tinkers commandeer buses and cause riotous mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinkers' looks like the noun for travelling menders, but here it is the verb: to monkey with something is to tinker with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is the idiom for playful or underhand trickery and pranks.

clue.text: Cow drover mistakenly put into enclosure lacking sufficient space

definitions.text: put into enclosure lacking sufficient space

indicators.note: doing something mistakenly means getting it wrong, so the letters of cow drover are set down in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A cattle drover wrongly herds his cows into a pen that is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges the nine letters of COW DROVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcrowd is to pack too many people or animals into a space, leaving them too little room.

clue.text: Knight, sporting Welsh national emblem, rising to adopt submissive stance before king

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the knight is wearing the emblem, so the two are joined with one tucked into the other

parts.note: the leek is a national emblem of Wales, worn on St David's Day
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight wearing a leek stands up, then bows low before his monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' puts N inside LEEK to give LEENK, and 'rising' turns that round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on one knee is the traditional posture of submission in front of a monarch.

clue.text: Plaintive howl might upset setter's keeper, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: might as a verb, as in 'it may rain', gives may
the setter refers to themself as me; the 's is read as has, linking to the next piece
a keeper ring is worn to hold a wedding ring in place, so a keeper is a type of ring

explanation.surface: A dog's mournful howling could annoy whoever looks after a gun dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MAY into YAM. 'setter' tempts you toward a dog; here it is the compiler, giving ME, whose keeper is a RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Yammering is loud persistent wailing or complaining, a mournful moaning cry.

clue.text: Tear open University Don's last monumental letters

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word Don's

parts.note: RIP, for rest in peace, is carved on gravestones and memorials

explanation.surface: A university lecturer's final inscription on a monument.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP (requiescat in pace) is the inscription on many tombstones.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrip is an old verb meaning to rip apart or slit open.

clue.text: Laying in cheap metal trashy signet rings

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the rearranged letters surround the metal
something trashy is shoddy and wrecked, so the letters of signet are knocked into a new order

parts.note: tin is an inexpensive base metal

explanation.surface: Cheap tin jewellery: tacky signet rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trashy' rearranges the signet letters to INSETG, and the metal goes in near the end, before the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Insetting is setting one thing into another, such as a panel or a stone placed into a surround.

clue.text: Cheer heart of sorrel at Epsom

indicators.note: the heart of a phrase is the stretch inside it, so the letters sit concealed within sorrel at Epsom

explanation.surface: A chestnut horse lifts spirits at Epsom racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: A sorrel is a reddish-brown horse, and Epsom is an English racecourse, home of the Derby; the letters run across sorrEL AT Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate someone is to fill them with joy, raising their spirits.

clue.text: Hamlet's rest from then on interrupted by the French

indicators.note: one word broken into by another, the second sitting in the middle of the first

parts.note: since means from that time onwards
le is the masculine form of the in French

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet's death scene, interrupted by a French intrusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's dying words are 'the rest is silence', so the definition is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's final line equates the rest that follows death with quiet and the absence of speech.

clue.text: Spring of quiet snow leopard

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: A quiet snow leopard leaps on its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to leap suddenly to seize something, a sudden spring.

clue.text: Daisy's neat look

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox is one
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy has a tidy appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy; it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy is a common wild flower of meadows, a white-petalled marguerite.

clue.text: Plant materials reassembled

indicators.note: something reassembled is put back together in a different way, so the letters of materials are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Factory components put back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassembled' rearranges MATERIALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's-tail is an aquatic plant with whorled leaves, sometimes also used for horsetails.

clue.text: Sodium dichromate ultimately sealing small cavity in aircraft casing

indicators.note: the last letter closes off the cavity, coming at its end like a seal

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a cell is a small compartment or cavity

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of dichromate

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a sodium compound used to seal a gap in a plane's casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sealing' puts the last letter of dichromate (from 'ultimately') after CELL, closing it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing on an aircraft that holds an engine.

clue.text: Model girl's rear's not small

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name

indicators.note: not tells us to take the letter away from the word for rear

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A model's backside is described as not small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes S from STERN, leaving TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a template or exemplar to be copied, as a model is.

clue.text: Predator lurking in alien warship

indicators.note: the predator is hiding inside the other word

parts.note: ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film, stands for an alien
the boa is a predatory snake

explanation.surface: A predator hides aboard an alien battleship, like a science-fiction film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Predator' suggests the film of that name, but here it is the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a fast German torpedo boat used in the Second World War.

clue.text: Privately support hosting meal over Vietnamese New Year

indicators.note: the support holds the other letters inside it, as a host holds guests

parts.note: a tee is a small peg supporting a golf ball

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the meal comes before the festival

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal
Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival

explanation.surface: Quietly backing a dinner held for the Vietnamese New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet is the lunar new year festival celebrated in Vietnam; in a down clue 'over' means coming above, so first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, so the adverb means in private, one to one.

clue.text: Demonstrate involvement of rascal caught engaged in packing deception

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or rascal

indicators.note: the word for deception is packed around the other letters

parts.note: a lie is a deception
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
at can mean busy with, as in at work or at play

explanation.surface: Showing someone's part in a con: a rogue caught up in a tangle of lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packing' puts CAT, built from C and AT, inside the deception, giving LICATE after the rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show that they are involved in a crime or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Temple at that time protected by flexible apron

indicators.note: the word is shielded by the letters around it, sitting inside them
something flexible bends into new shapes, so the letters of apron are reshaped

parts.note: then means at that time

explanation.surface: A temple of old, shielded by an adaptable apron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges the apron letters as PARON, and 'protected by' sets the time word inside after PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the ancient Greek temple to Athena on the Acropolis in Athens.

clue.text: Intricate caper about passport, possibly one containing nothing irregular

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the rest
an intricate arrangement is tangled, so the letters of caper are worked into a new order
the letters for passport and one hold the nothing inside them

parts.note: a passport is one example of an ID document
O looks like zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complicated caper involving a passport, perhaps one with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' gives IODI, with nothing inside passport plus one; 'Intricate' gives APERC from the caper letters, and 'about' wraps that round IODI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aperiodic means not occurring at regular intervals, without a repeating cycle.

clue.text: Veteran former England cricketer gets a run out

parts.note: Chris Old was a fast bowler for England in the 1970s and early 1980s

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of gets a with the run are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An ageing ex-England player is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GETS A plus R into STAGER. 'run out' reads as cricket dismissal, but 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is someone long experienced in an activity, a seasoned hand.

clue.text: Rejected Open Air Theatre players?

parts.note: out can mean outdoors, in the open air
the cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors turned down by an outdoor theatre company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open Air Theatre' reads as one venue, but it splits after Air.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone shunned or cast aside, so the word describes a person who has been rejected.

clue.text: Welcome cry

definitions.meaning: to welcome someone is to receive them with a hello
in Scots, to ... is to weep

explanation.definitionFit: To greet is to receive a visitor warmly, and in Scots dialect it also means to weep.

clue.text: Batting hero, not No. 2, English runs accumulator

indicators.note: the batsman's name loses its second letter, so the run letter is no longer in second place but goes to the end

parts.note: Jonathan Trott was England's batting star in the 2010-11 Ashes series
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A star batsman who is not the second in the order piles up English runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not No. 2' takes R, the second letter, out of TROTT; with E added it returns as the run at the end. Jonathan Trott was an England batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tots things up, adding them into a running total, is a gatherer of figures.

clue.text: Birds, two for one

parts.note: the tit and the lark are both birds, giving two pieces
the tit and the lark are both birds, giving two pieces

explanation.surface: Two birds offered for the price of one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two for one' says the two bird names together make a single bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The titlark is another name for the pipit, a small songbird, so the single word names a single bird.

clue.text: Mashed treat?

indicators.note: mashing squashes something into a new form, so the letters of treat are crushed into a new order

explanation.surface: Mashed potato as a comfort food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mashed' rearranges TREAT; the whole clue also describes a mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Tater is informal for potato, which mashed is a favourite comfort dish.

clue.text: Kermit, oddly enough, left the last bit of all seafood

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of Kermit, the first, third and fifth
the last bit of points to the final letter of all

explanation.surface: Kermit the Frog has, strangely, eaten up all the seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' takes KRI from Kermit; 'the last bit of' takes L from all.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny crustaceans eaten by whales and also harvested from the sea.

clue.text: Targets for elimination from Top 40

definitions.meaning: people marked down to be got rid of
a chart of the forty best-selling records

explanation.definitionFit: A hit list names people marked for killing or removal, and a chart of best-selling songs is literally a list of hits.

clue.text: Continuously sound essence of rhythmic spirit

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letters of rhythmic are taken

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Playing on, steadily sounding the core of a rhythmic spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essence of' takes TH, the middle two letters of rhythmic.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrum is to strum or drum monotonously, making a steady humming noise.

clue.text: This could be ultimately faint halo in NE

definitions.text: This could be ultimately faint halo in NE

indicators.note: could be says these letters might form something else when rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of faint

explanation.surface: A dim halo spotted in the north-east sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges T (the last letter of faint, from 'ultimately') with HALO IN NE; the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthelion is a faint bright spot or halo seen in the sky opposite the sun.

clue.text: Section extracted from bird's crest

indicators.note: the section is pulled out of the bird's name

parts.note: the partridge is a game bird
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A bit cut from a bird's plumed crest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' removes PART from PARTRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow crest, as of a hill or roof.

clue.text: Unwelcome visitors after treble hind cut?

definitions.text: Unwelcome visitors after treble hind cut?

indicators.note: after places the visitors at the end
cut shuffles the letters of treble hind as a deck of cards is cut

parts.note: mice are unwanted guests in a house

explanation.surface: Pests arriving after a deer has been sliced up three times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' rearranges TREBLE HIND to give THREEBLIND. In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the mice's tails, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme trio of rodents had their tails chopped off by a farmer's wife with a carving knife.
